response: Yes, mesopic pupil size can be measured with the cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method. This method involves using a cobalt blue light filter on a slit-lamp biomicroscope to constrict the pupil and then measuring the pupil size under mesopic (low-light) conditions. The cobalt blue light stimulates the intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells, allowing for a more accurate measurement of the pupil size in low-light environments.
